game.title: The Glade
start.welcome: 🌿 Welcome to The Glade. You wake up in a clearing surrounded by endless stone walls. Nobody remembers how they got here. Inside — survivors. Outside — the Maze. Type /help to see commands.
start.already: You are already in the Glade, {name}.
move.no_exit: You cannot go to «{target}» from here.
where.not_found: No such player in the Glade.

✅ Language: English.

Type /start again to wake up in the Glade.
loc.center.name: 🔥 Center / Bonfire
loc.center.desc: A vast clearing ringed by four grey stone walls, thick with ivy. In the centre burns a fire that never goes out. Smoke hangs in the air, and something older — the smell of stone that has never seen the sun.
The ivy on the walls shifts — not from wind, but on its own. Or so it seems. In the middle of the clearing lies a trampled circle, ringed by rough log benches. No one is here, but someone just left.
The walls rise hundreds of feet, closing off the sky on almost every side. Only a strip of light remains above. It smells of stone and earth. And of silence — the kind that hums.
On the edge of the clearing hangs a board with scraps of paper nailed to it. Someone was drawing a map and stopped halfway. The wind lifts a corner, and the map seems to breathe.
The fire crackles, but the sparks fall downward instead of rising. Someone once said it's because of the walls. That here, even fire behaves differently.
In the corner of the clearing stands a box sunk into the ground. It is empty. On the lid — scratched marks. Counting days. Many days.
The ivy on the wall forms a strange pattern — almost letters. You stare for a long time but cannot read it. Perhaps it is only ivy.
On the far edge — a circle of trampled grass. Nothing grows inside it. No one walks through it. And yet the grass is trampled.
A low hum drifts through — not from here. It comes from somewhere beyond the walls. Steady, like breathing. It never stops, day or night.
The walls are covered in ivy so thick in places they look green. In others — bare stone, grey and cold. The line between them is sharp, as if drawn by a hand.
loc.farms.name: 🌾 Farms
loc.farms.desc: Even rows of beds stretch all the way to the wall. The soil is dark, rich, damp to the touch. The ivy here grows lower — someone trimmed it back to let the light through.
It smells of earth and green things. Somewhere water drips — leaf to leaf, rhythmic. Wooden stakes stick out of the beds, with scraps of cloth tied to them. Markers.
The greenhouse in the corner is covered with fogged film. Something is inside — dark shapes, too large for plants. You do not open the door.
One bed breaks off abruptly, as if torn out. Beyond it — trampled earth, tracks leading to the wall and not coming back.
At the edge of the field lies an old watering can, grown into the ground. Beside it — a rag doll. Its face is worn away, but the eyes remain: two black dots.
The earth is bulging in places — as if something moved beneath it. Recently. You do not touch that spot.
The wall here is covered unevenly — patches of bare stone where the ivy has died. On the stone are scratches. Deep. As if someone tried to break through.
In the far corner — a wooden crate of tools. Spades, hoes. All in place. But no one is working. There is only the smell of earth.
You notice the beds form a pattern — if seen from above. Almost a letter. Almost a word. You are not sure.
The silence here is thick. Even footsteps sound muffled, as if the earth swallows sound. Somewhere at the edge of the field, the ivy moves.
loc.forge.name: ⚒️ Forge
loc.forge.desc: The forge is still warm — embers glow orange. The anvil stands in the centre, a hammer on top. No one is here, but the heat has not left. Someone was here a minute ago.
It smells of hot metal and coal. The walls of the forge are black with soot — not stone, but wood, charred. No ivy grows here. Too hot.
Tools hang on the walls: tongs, hammers, hooks. One hook is bent. On it — traces of something that is not metal. You do not touch it.
In the corner — a barrel of water. The water is black, oily. A rainbow film floats on the surface. Someone left something here they did not want to see.
On the floor — fragments. Not metal. Stone, but too smooth, as if polished. No such stone exists in the Glade. They came from the Maze.
The forge hums — not with fire, but with something deeper. The sound comes from beneath the ground. You press your palm to the floor. It is warm.
Names are scratched into the wall. Three. Beneath each — a date. The dates are old. One name is circled twice. You do not know why.
It smells not only of metal. Something else lingers — iron and salt. Like blood, but old, dried. You push the thought away.
The forge stands closest to the eastern wall. From here the hum of the Maze is audible — low, rhythmic. It echoes in the anvil if you put your ear to it.
The hammer on the anvil is not lying the way it usually does. The handle points toward the exit. As if someone dropped it in a hurry. You do not move it.
loc.medbay.name: 🏥 Medbay
loc.medbay.desc: The tent is stretched between two posts. The flap moves — though there is no wind. Inside it smells of herbs, alcohol, and something sweet, cloying.
A jacket lies on the cot. A hole in the chest. The blood has dried, turned brown. The jacket is folded neatly. Its owner is gone.
In the corner — a crate of tools. Scalpels, needles, vials. One vial is empty. The stopper is in place, but the contents are gone.
The tent wall — from the inside — is covered in scratches. Someone was counting. You count twenty-three. Then the scratches stop.
It smells of herbs, but not only. There is a scent you cannot name. It is not from the Glade. It is from the Maze. You are certain.
A map lies unrolled on the table. The lines are crooked, broken off. In the corner — a signature. You cannot read it. The letters do not look like any you know.
The cot is made. The sheet is clean. Too clean. As if just changed. But no one came in. You would have noticed.
A bag hangs on the wall. Inside — a flask and something wrapped in cloth. You do not unwrap it. The smell is too familiar.
The medical tools are laid out in perfect order. Too perfect. As if someone was not working, but arranging them. For something.
In the corner of the tent — a bucket. Inside — a rag. The rag is pink. The water is pink. You turn away.
loc.huts.name: 🏠 Huts
loc.huts.desc: The huts stand close together, wall to wall. The wood is dark, damp. The ivy from the Glade walls has climbed onto the roofs — some roofs are green.
Inside one hut — a cot. The blanket is crumpled. The pillow still holds a dent. Whoever slept here left recently. Or was taken.
A jacket hangs on a hook by the entrance. Something is in the pocket. You do not check. The pocket bulges, as if holding something angular.
Scattered papers cover the floor. Scrawls, lines, arrows. A map. One line leads to the wall and stops. The paper is crumpled, as if squeezed in a fist.
In the corner — a chest. The lid is ajar. Inside — rags, a flask. And something glinting. You do not step closer. It smells of dust and something else.
The walls of the huts are thin. You hear breathing — steady, calm. Someone is asleep. But when you look in — the cot is empty. The blanket is smooth.
Scratches on the wall. Marks. Many. You count thirty-one. Then more. Someone counted for a very long time. And then stopped.
It smells of damp wood and moss. Somewhere water drips — rhythmic. Drip. Drip. Drip. You look for the source but cannot find it. The sound comes from inside the wall.
The door of one hut is boarded shut. From the inside. You do not try to open it. The boards are fresh. The nails are shiny.
The huts are arranged in a circle. If you stand in the centre and turn — every door faces the fire. All doors are closed. All but one.
loc.south_gates.name: 🚪 South Gates
loc.south_gates.desc: The southern wall is lower than the rest — or so it seems, because of the ivy. It is thickest here, darkest. The gates are open. Damp drifts from the gap.
On the ground at the entrance — names. Scratched with stone, with a knife, with fingernails. You read. One name is crossed out. Then another. Then all of them are crossed out.
It does not smell of stone here. It smells of water — stagnant, musty. Like a well into which something fell. Long ago.
You hear footsteps. Slow, heavy. They come toward the gates. You wait. The footsteps fade. No one emerges.
The stone at the entrance is covered with something — not moss, not mould. A grey film. You touch it with a finger. The film stays on your skin. You wipe it on your trousers.
The South Gates are the oldest — you can tell from the stone. It is chipped, cracked. Moisture seeps from the cracks. The wall weeps.
On the doors — marks. Not from knives. From fingernails. Someone clawed at the stone from the inside. The marks are deep. Fresh.
You notice that the ivy at the South Gates does not reach into the Maze. It grows to the edge of the gap and stops. As if it does not want to.
Something gleams in the darkness of the gap. Metal. Small. You do not approach. You do not want to know what it is.
The hum is quieter here than in the north. Or deeper. It echoes in your chest rather than your ears. You feel it, not hear it.

loc.north_gates.name: 🚪 North Gates
loc.north_gates.desc: Four vast stone walls, wrapped in ivy, form the Glade. In the northern wall — a gap. It is open. Beyond it — the darkness of the Maze.
The ivy above the North Gates is thickest — someone once said it grows faster on this side. You do not know if that is true. But the ivy here is almost black.
Cold drifts from the gap. Not wind — something else. The temperature drops a few degrees as you approach. You feel it on your skin.
On the stones at the entrance — scratches. Names. You read one. Then a second. Then you stop. The list is too long.
A hum. It comes from the Maze. Low, steady, like a heartbeat. It never stops. You realise you have heard it all along, you simply never noticed.
The gap is open. Beyond it — walls. Grey, like those outside. But there they move. You do not see the movement, but you feel it. The walls are alive.
On the ground at the gates — a rope. Knots at even intervals. Someone was counting paces. The rope breaks off at the very edge of the gap. Beyond it, nothing.
You press your palm against the stone at the entrance. The stone is warm. Not like earth — like something alive. You pull your hand back.
Something emerges from the gap — not cloth, not paper. Something thin, grey. It lies on the stone. You do not touch it.
The ivy above the gates shifts. There is no wind. You watch it. It goes still. You turn away. It moves again.
loc.west_gates.name: 🚪 West Gates
loc.west_gates.desc: The western wall is the darkest. Ivy covers it almost entirely, leaving only a narrow gap. Inside — blackness. Not a flicker of light.
The gap of the West Gates is warped. The stones at its edges have been forced outward. As if something tried to seal it from the inside. And failed.
You stand ten paces away and do not want to come closer. Not fear — instinct. Something in the darkness is watching you. You do not know what.
It smells of water. Not rain — standing water. Like a cellar whose windows have not been opened in years. The smell comes from the gap, steady and heavy.
A green film coats the stones at the entrance. Damp. Slimy. You do not touch it. Does the film pulse? No. It is a shadow of ivy.
A sound comes from the gap. Not a hum. Dripping. Rhythmic, slow. Drip. Pause. Drip. Pause. You count. Twelve. Then silence.
The West Gates are unguarded. There are no footprints here. None at all. As if no one ever approaches. Or those who do leave no tracks.
You see something on the ground. A dark stain. Long. It stretches toward the gates. You do not follow it. You leave.
The gap is open, but the darkness within does not thin. Light does not enter. You wave a hand — the shadow does not move.
The ivy at the West Gates is dry. Dead. The branches are brittle, grey. You break one off. It crumbles to dust. The wall behind it is grey too.
loc.east_gates.name: 🚪 East Gates
loc.east_gates.desc: The eastern wall is the smoothest. There is almost no ivy — only near the base, in sparse patches. The stone here gleams, as if polished.
The gap of the East Gates hums. You hear it from a distance. A low, rhythmic sound. Like a heart beating not in a chest, but in the wall.
You press your palm against the stone at the entrance. The stone vibrates. Fine, rapid. Like machinery working somewhere far away. Or close.
It does not smell of stone from the gap. It smells of a storm. Ozone. The hair on your arms rises, though you feel no cold.
On the stones at the entrance — symbols. Carved deep. They resemble nothing you know. You stare for a long time. One symbol seems familiar. You do not remember.
Metal. The East Gates have metal — flecks embedded in the stone. You have not seen this elsewhere. The metal is warm. You do not touch it twice.
You hear a whisper. Not from the gap — inside your head. The words are indistinct. The voice is a woman's. Young. You look around. No one.
The gap is open. Inside — walls. They move. You catch it from the corner of your eye. When you look straight — they are still. You do not trust your eyes.
On the ground at the entrance — a metal sphere. Smooth. It is warm. You do not pick it up. It has lain here a long time. Dust does not settle around it.
The hum intensifies. For a second. Then fades. You feel that something has happened. Something has changed. You do not know what. You leave faster than you planned.

maze.look.danger: ⚠️ You touched something. A stone falls from the wall. −{dmg} HP.
maze.section.corridor: A sloped corridor descends into darkness. The floor is slick with moisture, the walls cracked. Something dark seeps from the cracks — not water. You try not to touch the walls.
A narrow passage between two stone slabs. It smells of damp and something iron. Your footsteps echo twice — as if someone else is walking.
The corridor winds. You lose count of the turns. Somewhere far off, water drips — rhythmic, like a metronome. Drip. Pause. Drip.
The walls here are covered in ivy — dry, dead. It crunches underfoot. You notice the ivy trails in one direction — as if something dragged it.
A dark corridor. Light barely seeps through — from where, unclear. Dust hangs in the air, unmoving. You pass through it.
The corridor widens and narrows for no reason. You hear breathing — but it's your own echo. Probably.
Cold air. You see your own breath. The walls are covered in frost — though it's warm outside.
The corridor is straight as an arrow. Too straight. You feel watched. You turn — no one.
The stone walls are covered in scratches. Not from knives — from fingernails. Someone tried to break through. Long ago.
You enter the corridor, and the sound of your steps changes. They fall duller now, as if the earth swallows sound.
maze.section.hall: A vast hall. The ceiling is lost in darkness. The echo returns late — as if the hall is larger than it seems.
A spacious hall of pillars. Symbols are carved into the floor. You cannot read them, but you sense they are old.
A round hall. The hum is louder here. It echoes in your chest, not your ears.
Broken statues line the walls. Their faces have been worn away — by someone who did not want them recognised.
A high vaulted hall. Something moves in the shadows above. You do not look up.
The floor is cracked. Beneath it — darkness. You do not check what lies below.
A grand hall, abandoned for ages. Dust hangs in the air, never settling.
Stone slabs on the floor form a pattern. It resembles a map. You cannot read it.
maze.section.dead_end: A dead end. No way forward. The wall is smooth, as if polished.
A wall. You must turn back. You hear something behind it — scratching.
A blind alcove. Only stone. And silence.
A stone pocket. Nothing here. And no one.
The passage ends abruptly. The wall is smooth and cold. You do not want to stay here.
maze.section.junction: A fork. Several paths diverge from here. You hear footsteps — but not your own.
A crossroads. You sense many have passed through. The stone is worn.
A junction. Which way? The echo hints — but it lies.
Three tunnels meet here. The air is still. Each one smells different.
A branching point. Every path looks the same. But you know — they are not.
maze.section.center: You stand at the very heart of the Maze. The walls move here — you feel it on your skin. The hum never stops.
The central hall. The ceiling is unseen. The floor is warm — too warm for stone.
The core of the Maze. Something is watching. You cannot see it, but you know. The hair on your arms rises.
The centre. It is quiet here — but not like other places. This is the silence before something.

loc.kitchen.name: 🍲 Kitchen
loc.kitchen.desc: It smells of boiled meat and herbs. Something simmers on the stove, steam escaping through cracks. A table by the wall is covered with roots and herbs — someone is cooking seriously. A man in an apron stands at the stove, stirring a pot without looking up.
loc.dining.name: 🍽️ Dining Hall
loc.dining.desc: Long wooden tables, rough benches. It smells of food and smoke. Names are scratched into the walls — who ate here, who left and did not return. In the corner — an empty mug. No one touches it.
loc.council.name: 🏛️ Council
loc.council.desc: A small hut, but surprisingly serious inside. A long table where the fate of the Glade is decided. On the walls — a map of the Maze, covered in notes. It smells of ink, wax, and something else — the weight of decisions.
loc.watchtower.name: 🗼 Watchtower
loc.watchtower.desc: A wooden tower by the north wall. From here you can see the whole Glade and a piece of the Maze beyond the gates. Someone is always on top, watching. The wind is stronger here, and it smells of stone — alien and cold.
loc.storage.name: 📦 Storage
loc.storage.desc: A dark shed packed with crates, barrels, and sacks. It smells of dust, grain, and something iron. On the shelves — tools, ropes, old things. Half of it is unsorted. No one wants to know what is inside.
loc.well.name: 💧 Well
loc.well.desc: A stone well in the center of a small clearing. The water is cold and clean — the only relief in this place. On the frame — scratched marks: someone counted buckets, someone — days. In the depths of the well — darkness, too deep for an ordinary well.
loc.workshop.name: 🔧 Workshop
loc.workshop.desc: A cramped room cluttered with tools and fragments. It smells of metal, sawdust, and machine oil. On the workbench — unfinished mechanisms, blueprints, fragments of something unclear. The owner seems to have been taking apart something very strange.
loc.graveyard.name: ⚰️ Graveyard
loc.graveyard.desc: A small plot of land by the south wall. Five wooden crosses driven into the ground. On each — a name carved with a knife. Some are already worn away. It smells of earth and wet wood. It is quiet here. Even the wind does not come here.
loc.garden.name: 🌿 Garden
loc.garden.desc: A small plot separated from the farms. Strange plants grow here — not like those on the farms. Someone grows them separately. It smells of herbs, bitter and unfamiliar. At the edge — a bed of flowers. No one knows who planted them.
loc.training.name: 🎯 Training Ground
loc.training.desc: A cleared patch of ground by the west wall. Straw dummies, wooden swords, targets made of old boards. It smells of sweat and dust. Someone trained here before you. Someone, perhaps, did not survive their training.

npc.frypan.name: 🍳 Frypan
npc.frypan.desc: The Glade's cook. Grumpy, but kind.
npc.frypan.dialog: "Newcomer? Sit down, have a bite. Don't thank me for food — it's all shared. Well... almost all. What do you need?"
npc.clint.name: 🔨 Clint
npc.jeff.name: 💊 Jeff
npc.jeff.desc: Medic. Tired, but always ready to help.
npc.jeff.dialog: "Wounds? Sit down. Bear it — it will hurt."
npc.minho.name: 🏃 Minho
npc.minho.desc: Leader of the Runners. Knows the Maze best.
npc.minho.dialog: "Run? Good. I'll show you where we've been. Listen carefully — I won't repeat."
npc.minho.no_map: No one has discovered anything yet.
npc.chuck.name: 🧒 Chuck
npc.chuck.desc: The youngest in the Glade. Friendly and curious.
npc.chuck.dialog: "Hi! You're new, right? I was new too. Want a hint?"
npc.chuck.hint.1: 💡 Don't go into the Maze without torches — it's dark.
npc.chuck.hint.2: 💡 Food and water are consumed in the Maze. Take extra.
npc.chuck.hint.3: 💡 If you see a Griever — don't fight it alone.
npc.chuck.hint.4: 💡 Sleep restores HP and energy. Don't forget to sleep.
npc.chuck.hint.5: 💡 The Maze is more dangerous at night. Day is better.
npc.alby.name: 👴 Alby
npc.alby.desc: The first Glader. Leader. Wise and just.
npc.alby.dialog: "You came. Sit. Tell me — what do you need from the Council?"
npc.winston.name: 🌾 Winston
npc.winston.dialog: "Here to work? Good. Just don't spare your hands — the earth doesn't like that."
npc.newt.name: 🧑 Newt
npc.newt.dialog: "What do you need? If it's business — speak. If not — don't bother me."
npc.gally.name: 😠 Gally
npc.gally.dialog: "What are you staring at? Think you're special? They all came like that. Where are they now?"

time.cmd.hint: The Maze is dangerous at night. Grievers are 50% stronger.
loc.center.desc.dawn: The fire has burned down — only embers glow. First rays of light seep through cracks in the walls. Someone is already up, walking around the clearing. Morning is the only quiet time in the Glade.
loc.center.desc.day: The day is in full swing. The fire is out, smoke barely visible. Around — life: someone carries water, someone sits by the wall sharpening a knife. The Glade works.
loc.center.desc.dusk: The sun sets. Shadows grow long. Someone already lights the fire — first sparks fly up. People speak quieter, glancing at the walls.
loc.center.desc.night: The fire is the only light. Shadows dance on the walls, trembling, as if alive. Everyone sits closer to the fire. Somewhere beyond the wall — a low hum. The Maze is awake.
loc.kitchen.desc.dawn: The kitchen smells of fresh bread. Someone already lit the stove. Quiet, only the crackle of wood.
loc.kitchen.desc.day: The kitchen is in full swing: boiling, hissing, chopping. Frypan is yelling at someone. It smells so good it makes your mouth water.
loc.kitchen.desc.dusk: The kitchen quiets down. Food is almost ready. Last rays of sun fall on the table.
loc.kitchen.desc.night: The kitchen is dark — only dying embers in the stove give light. It smells of old food and smoke. No one lingers here at night.
loc.watchtower.desc.dawn: From the height you can see the Maze waking up. For a moment the walls seem calm. At dawn they do not move — or so it seems.
loc.watchtower.desc.day: During the day you can see the Runners returning. Short shadows, gray walls. The wind rustles uneasily.
loc.watchtower.desc.dusk: Sunset paints the Maze walls crimson. It seems the walls are breathing. Below, someone lights the fire.
loc.watchtower.desc.night: At night only black silhouettes of walls are visible from the tower. The hum of the Maze is louder. Looking there hurts. The watchmen give up and come down.
loc.north_gates.desc.dawn: At dawn the gates seem calm. Ivy glistens with dew. Guards stretch after the night shift.
loc.north_gates.desc.day: During the day it is busy at the gates — Runners gather before going out, checking gear. The hum of the Maze is muffled, but never silent.
loc.north_gates.desc.dusk: Dusk thickens. The gate leaves tremble — as if something pushes from inside. Guards are tense. Closing soon.
loc.north_gates.desc.night: At night the gates are closed. Behind them footsteps — heavy, slow, inhuman. No one goes out. No one looks into the gap.
sleep.in_maze: No one sleeps in the Maze. Here, sleeping ones are found — and not woken.

intro.step_dark: 🌑 Darkness. You don't remember how you got here. You don't remember where you came from. Only a voice in your head — alien, but familiar: "Run. Remember. Survive."
intro.step_wake: ☁️ Awakening. You open your eyes. Above — a grey sky. Metal bars of a cage. Light pierces through them. The cage rises. Slowly.
intro.step_cage: 🔓 Arrival. The grate opens. Above you — faces. Many faces. Teenagers. They watch silently — some with curiosity, some with worry. One of them — a guy with light hair — offers his hand.
intro.step_arrive: 🧑 Newt: "Get up. I'm Newt. Welcome to the Glade." He looks at you intently, as if studying you. "Listen. Everyone here is the same — no one remembers how they got here. But everyone remembers why they want out. Do you?"
intro.step_q1: 🧑 Newt: "Alright. Tell me: why do you want out?" Choose your motivation.
perk.revenge.name: Revenge
perk.revenge.desc: I will find who did this. +10% damage.
perk.freedom.name: Freedom
perk.freedom.desc: I just want to see the sky. +5 energy.
perk.truth.name: Truth
perk.truth.desc: I want to know what this place is. +5% fragment chance.
perk.home.name: Home
intro.step_q2: 🧑 Newt: "Fine. Now the main thing. You will go into the Maze. Sooner or later. Everyone goes. What could you do before you forgot everything?"
prof.fighter.name: Fighter
prof.fighter.desc: Fought. Can stand up for myself. +10 HP, +2 damage.
prof.engineer.name: Engineer
prof.engineer.desc: Worked with my hands. Can fix anything. Compass + craft bonus.
prof.medic.name: Medic
prof.medic.desc: Healed people. Know herbs. +10 HP, stronger healing (+5 HP per bandage).
prof.scout.name: Scout
prof.scout.desc: Ran. No one was faster. +10 energy, +5% flee chance.
intro.step_gift: 🧑 Newt: "Take this. It's all I can give. The rest — on your own." He hands you:
loc.abandoned_hut.name: 🏚️ Abandoned Hut
loc.abandoned_hut.desc: A hut on the edge of the Glade. Walls covered in moss, roof sagging. The door is ajar — cold and something else, unfamiliar, drifts from inside. No one comes here. They say Teresa lives here.
loc.abandoned_hut.desc.day: By day the hut seems almost ordinary — just old, forgotten. But the shadow at the door does not move with the sun. Someone is watching from inside.
loc.abandoned_hut.desc.night: At night the hut looks ominous. A weak light seeps through the cracks — not from fire. The door is ajar. Teresa is not sleeping.
hint.abandoned_hut: Teresa lives here. She knows what others do not.
npc.teresa.name: 🌙 Teresa
npc.teresa.desc: A girl with dark hair. Her eyes are too calm for this place.
npc.teresa.dialog:
"You came. I've been waiting."

She looks at you without blinking. In her eyes — something the others do not have.

"I know why the Maze was built. Want to find out? You'll have to work."
story.title: STORY QUESTS
story.giver_intro.alby: "Got a job for you. Listen carefully."
story.giver_intro.minho: "Want to run? First show me what you can do."
story.giver_intro.teresa: "I know what they don't. But first — I'll test you."
story.no_quests: All done for now. Come back later.
story.quest.first_step.title: 🌱 First Step
story.quest.first_step.desc: Alby: "Go into the Maze. Once. Just look. And come back — if you can."
story.quest.find_minho.title: 🏃 Find Minho
story.quest.find_minho.desc: Alby: "Find Minho. He's at the Watchtower. He'll tell you more than I will."
story.quest.recon.title: 🔍 Recon
story.quest.recon.desc: Minho: "Walk through three Maze sections. Don't memorize — just look. Then tell me."
story.quest.fragment_hunt.title: 🗺️ Map Fragment
story.quest.fragment_hunt.desc: Minho: "Find a map fragment. First one. You'll understand why later."
story.quest.find_teresa.title: 🌙 Find Teresa
story.quest.find_teresa.desc: Minho: "There's one... Teresa. She's in the abandoned hut. Talk to her."
story.quest.teresa_secret.title: 🤫 Teresa's Secret
story.quest.teresa_secret.desc: Teresa: "Bring me Key 3. I'll tell you what I know."
story.quest.voice_of_maze.title: 🐺 Voice of the Maze
story.quest.voice_of_maze.desc: Teresa: "Kill five Grievers. And listen. The Maze whispers when they die."
story.quest.through_walls.title: 🌀 Through the Walls
story.quest.through_walls.desc: Teresa: "Reach the Maze Center. Not for fragments — just reach it. And look at the walls."
story.quest.keys_of_gates.title: 🗝️ Keys of the Gates
story.quest.keys_of_gates.desc: Teresa: "Collect three keys. Any. First step to the Gates."
story.quest.path_to_gates.title: 🌟 Path to the Gates
story.quest.path_to_gates.desc: Teresa: "Collect all five keys. And open the Gates. Then you'll know everything."
story.stage.arrived.name: 🌿 Arrival
story.stage.arrived.desc: You are in the Glade. Time to learn more.
story.stage.met_alby.name: 👴 Meeting Alby
story.stage.met_alby.desc: Alby entrusted you with your first task.
story.stage.met_minho.name: 🏃 Meeting Minho
story.stage.met_minho.desc: Minho — leader of Runners. He knows the Maze.
story.stage.met_teresa.name: 🌙 Meeting Teresa
story.stage.met_teresa.desc: Teresa knows more than she says.
story.stage.learned_truth.name: 🤫 Learned the Truth
story.stage.learned_truth.desc: You now know what others do not.
story.stage.final_ready.name: 🌟 Ready for the Gates
story.stage.final_ready.desc: You are ready to open the Gates.
